text:
[ISTS.7.1] Some spec claims are real but not
unit-testable. They go in the impl-suite (where
applicable), in static-analysis tooling, or in
review rules — never in `spec/`.

| Claim | Why not spec-testable | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| `IARC.1.10` "no threads, never blocks" | Structural — can grep, can't unit-test absence | Code review; CI grep |
| `IARC.1.11` "no globals" | Structural; can grep for non-`static` mutable file-scope decls | Code review |
| `IARC.1.13` "per-object malloc" | Structural — same | Code review |
| `IERR.4.1.1` "detail valid until next libds call" | Lifetime invariant — provable in specific scenarios but not in general | Impl tests for specific scenarios; doc |
| `LDET.3.4.1` cross-platform byte-identical replay | Needs two platform signatures at once, so it is a calibration run rather than a suite case | A calibration run: one corpus replayed on two platforms, and the two replays compared byte for byte |
| `LLOG.5` test CEs under logical | The test CE is already lowered correctly, and behavioural coverage rides on the `LLOG.1` obligation, whose fixture uses a `where` clause | [LLOG.14.2] |
| `LLOG.8` explicit retract of a logical fact | Compile time: DS has no `retract` verb, so the case is rejected there. Runtime: `ds_engine_retract` works on any schema | [LLOG.14.2] |
